title: 10  Scientists Who Were Their Own Guinea Pigs
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss scientists who experimented on themselves, counting down ten examples across history. They open with personal banter (Chuck's name change, Dark Matters on Science Channel, a Depeche Mode/Pet Shop Boys tangent) and cover Santorio Santorio's lifelong metabolism weighing, Friedrich Sertürner's morphine testing on himself and teenage friends, Henry Head's self-severed radial nerve study, Alexandre Shulgin's psychedelic drug self-experiments, Jan Evangelista Purkyně's self-dosing with ipecac, nightshade and carousel vertigo, George Stratton's inverting lenses for eight days, Karl Landsteiner's ABO blood typing and Jack Goldstein's enzyme-treated blood, and Hermann Ebbinghaus's memory experiments with nonsense syllables. They discuss the ethics and scientific limits of self-experimentation, the modern quantified self movement and Seth Roberts. The episode closes with a listener email about the Black Death and the origins of English, sources, and promotional plugs.

segments.title: Opening banter and Dark Matters promo
segments.summary: Chuck announces his name change and they joke about Jan-Michael Vincent. They promote the Science Channel show Dark Matters and tease the episode's theme of self-experimenting scientists.

segments.title: Overview and early self-experimenters
segments.summary: They introduce the list, mention related episodes on human experimentation and government experiments, and recap Albert Hofmann's first LSD trip and the knuckle-cracking doctor. They then describe Santorio Santorio's decades of weighing food, drink, and excrement to study metabolism and insensible perspiration.

segments.title: Sertürner and the discovery of morphine
segments.summary: Friedrich Sertürner isolated morphine from opium, tested it on animals, then dosed himself and three teenage friends. They became queasy and vomited, and he later found morphine relieved his toothache where opium did not.

segments.title: Henry Head's severed nerve
segments.summary: Henry Head and W.H.R. Rivers cut and resutured a section of Head's own radial nerve to document how sensation returns. Head used negative attitude of attention to focus on pain, which contributed to research on reverie. Chuck relates his root canal experience.

segments.title: Alexander Shulgin's psychedelic experiments
segments.summary: Alexander Shulgin, a chemist, tested psychoactive compounds, including mescaline and compounds related to MDMA, with his wife, and reportedly sampled 200 to 250 of an estimated 300 psychoactive compounds.

segments.title: Purkyně's self-dosing and vertigo
segments.summary: Jan Evangelista Purkyně became a doctor to test drug doses he thought were too low. He took foxglove, nightshade, and ipecac, and spun on carousels to study vertigo. Colleagues sought his help with testing extracts, and he later stopped self-experimenting to raise his sons.

segments.title: George Stratton's upside-down vision
segments.summary: George Stratton wore reversing lenses for eight days to test whether visual input must be inverted to be seen upright. He found the world looked upside down at first, then gradually adjusted, and needed time to readapt afterward. Later he used a single lens.

segments.title: Landsteiner's ABO blood types and Goldstein's universal blood
segments.summary: Karl Landsteiner identified ABO blood types, using his own and colleagues' blood, and won a Nobel Prize. Jack Goldstein later used an enzyme from coffee to convert type B blood to universal type O, testing it by receiving a small transfusion himself.

segments.title: Ebbinghaus's memory research and self-experimentation today
segments.summary: Hermann Ebbinghaus used nonsense syllables to study memory, measuring forgetting and relearning and documenting the learning curve and the value of spaced study over cramming. They discuss the Ebbinghaus illusion, the limits of self-experimentation in modern science, and Seth Roberts and the quantified self movement.

segments.title: Sources, plugs, and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts list sources, promote their Wyatt Cenac special and the Super Stuff Guide to Happiness audiobook, give the text-message podcast link, and read a listener email about the Black Death and the origins of English. They invite listener experiences with self-experimentation.
